disclaimer: These protocols are general education, not a diagnosis or a treatment plan. Progress only when movement is tolerable, and see a physician or physical therapist before starting if you have an acute injury, a recent surgery, or pain that is not improving.
pain_rule: Use the 0-10 traffic light: 0-3 during and settled by the next morning is acceptable, 4-5 means reduce load or range, 6+ or pain that lingers past 24 hours means stop and regress a phase.

knee.name: Knee
knee.summary: Knee rehab restores full extension first, then rebuilds quadriceps and hip strength, and finally reintroduces impact and single-leg load. Hip and ankle strength matter as much as the knee itself, because both control how the knee tracks under load.
common_conditions: Post-ACL or meniscus surgery, once cleared by a surgeon
precautions: Regaining full straight-leg extension early matters more than regaining deep bend; a knee that will not fully straighten changes how you walk.
Swelling that increases after a session is the clearest sign you did too much, even if pain felt fine at the time.
Avoid deep loaded knee bend and open-chain leg extension with heavy load during early patellofemoral or patellar tendon irritation.
red_flags: Cannot bear weight for four steps
Rapid, large swelling within an hour of injury
Obvious deformity, fever, or a hot, red joint

phases.name: Calm and Protect
phases.goal: Settle swelling, restore full extension, and wake the quadriceps back up.
phases.advance_when: Swelling is minimal, the knee straightens fully, and you can hold a straight-leg raise without the knee sagging.

exercises.name: Quad Set
exercises.description: Sit with the leg straight and press the back of the knee down into the floor, tightening the thigh so the kneecap glides up.
cues: Squeeze the thigh, do not hold your breath
Watch the kneecap slide toward your hip

exercises.name: Heel Prop for Extension
exercises.description: Rest the heel on a rolled towel with the knee unsupported and let gravity straighten the joint.
cues: Let the knee hang, stay relaxed
Stop if you feel sharp pain rather than a stretch

exercises.name: Heel Slide
exercises.description: Lying down, slide the heel toward the hip to a comfortable bend, then slide it back out.
cues: Move to the edge of discomfort, not through it
Use a strap or towel to assist if needed

exercises.name: Straight Leg Raise
exercises.description: With the knee locked straight, lift the whole leg to about 45 degrees and lower it under control.
cues: Set the quad before the leg leaves the floor
No knee sag on the way up

exercises.name: Ankle Pump
exercises.description: Point and flex the ankle rhythmically to drive swelling out of the lower leg.
cues: Full range each direction
Best done with the leg elevated

phases.name: Rebuild Strength
phases.goal: Load the knee through closed-chain movement and build the hip strength that controls it.
phases.advance_when: You can sit to stand from a low chair on one leg with control and walk 30 minutes without a flare.

exercises.name: Sit to Stand
exercises.description: Stand from a chair without using your hands, then lower back down over three seconds.
cues: Push evenly through both feet
The slow lowering is the point

exercises.name: Terminal Knee Extension
exercises.description: With a band pulling the back of the knee forward, straighten the knee against the band.
cues: Finish each rep fully locked out
Keep the heel down

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
exercises.description: Lying on your back with knees bent, drive through the heels and lift the hips until shoulders, hips, and knees line up.
cues: Squeeze the glutes at the top
Ribs down, do not arch the back

exercises.name: Low Step-Up
exercises.description: Step up onto a low box leading with the injured leg, then lower back down slowly.
cues: Knee tracks over the middle toes
Do not push off the trailing foot

exercises.name: Side-Lying Hip Abduction
exercises.description: Lying on your side, lift the top leg straight up with the toes pointed slightly down.
cues: Lead with the heel, not the toe
Do not roll the hips backward

exercises.name: Hamstring Slider Curl
exercises.description: In a bridge position, slide the heels away from you and pull them back in using the hamstrings.
cues: Keep the hips up the whole set
Shorten the range if you feel cramping

phases.name: Load and Return
phases.goal: Build single-leg strength and reintroduce impact so the knee tolerates sport and daily surprises.
phases.advance_when: Single-leg strength is within about 10 percent of the other side and hopping is pain free.

exercises.name: Split Squat
exercises.description: In a staggered stance, lower the back knee toward the floor and drive back up through the front leg.
cues: Torso tall, front shin roughly vertical
Add load only once bodyweight is easy

exercises.name: Eccentric Step-Down
exercises.description: Stand on a step on the injured leg and lower the other heel toward the floor over three seconds.
cues: Control the descent, tap lightly
Do not let the knee collapse inward

exercises.name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
exercises.description: Hinge at the hip on one leg, letting the free leg travel back as the chest lowers.
cues: Hips square to the floor
Feel it in the hamstring and glute, not the low back

exercises.name: Pogo Hop
exercises.description: Small, springy double-leg hops staying on the balls of the feet.
cues: Quiet landings, minimal knee bend
Stop the set if landings get noisy

exercises.name: Lateral Hop and Stick
exercises.description: Hop sideways onto one leg and hold the landing for two seconds without wobbling.
cues: Land softly, knee over the foot
Hold until fully still before the next rep

shoulder.name: Shoulder
shoulder.summary: Shoulder rehab restores pain-free motion, then trains the rotator cuff and the muscles that control the shoulder blade, and finally returns you to overhead and pressing load. Most stubborn shoulder pain improves when the shoulder blade starts moving well.
common_conditions: Rotator cuff tendinopathy or subacromial pain
precautions: In early phases, work below shoulder height; painful arcs overhead usually mean the tissue is not ready.
After a dislocation, avoid the combined position of abduction plus external rotation until cleared.
Pain down the arm past the elbow with numbness or tingling is a neck referral pattern and needs assessment, not shoulder strengthening.
red_flags: Cannot actively lift the arm at all after a trauma
Visible deformity or a suspected dislocation
Night pain with unexplained weight loss or fever
Progressive weakness or numbness in the hand

phases.name: Restore Motion
phases.goal: Reduce irritation and regain pain-free range below shoulder height.
phases.advance_when: You can raise the arm to shoulder height without a sharp catch and sleep through most nights.

exercises.name: Pendulum Swing
exercises.description: Lean on a table with the free arm hanging, and let it swing in small circles using body sway.
cues: The arm is passive, the body creates the motion
Small circles, stay relaxed

exercises.name: Scapular Setting
exercises.description: Gently draw the shoulder blades down and back without shrugging, and hold.
cues: Think back pocket, not shrug
Neck stays long and soft

exercises.name: Table Slide
exercises.description: Rest the forearm on a table and slide it forward, letting the chest drop to raise the arm without muscling it.
cues: Let the table carry the weight
Stop at the first pinch

exercises.name: Supine External Rotation
exercises.description: Lying down with the elbow tucked at 90 degrees, rotate the forearm outward to a comfortable range.
cues: Keep a towel under the elbow
Range before effort

exercises.name: Thoracic Extension over Towel
exercises.description: Lie back over a rolled towel placed across the mid-back and open the chest.
cues: Support the head
Breathe into the stretch for 3 breaths

phases.name: Cuff and Scapula
phases.goal: Build rotator cuff endurance and scapular control under light, controlled load.
phases.advance_when: Band work is easy for 15 controlled reps and you can raise the arm overhead without compensating.

exercises.name: Band External Rotation
exercises.description: With the elbow tucked at the side, rotate the forearm outward against a band.
cues: Elbow stays pinned to the ribs
Control the return, do not let the band snap back

exercises.name: Band Internal Rotation
exercises.description: Elbow tucked, rotate the forearm across the body against the band.
cues: Same tucked elbow position
Slow and smooth both directions

exercises.name: Band Row
exercises.description: Pull the band toward the ribs, finishing by drawing the shoulder blade back.
cues: Lead with the elbow
Do not shrug at the finish

exercises.name: Scaption Raise
exercises.description: Raise light weights to shoulder height at about 30 degrees in front of the body, thumbs up.
cues: Stop at shoulder height early on
Very light weight, this is control work

exercises.name: Wall Slide with Serratus Punch
exercises.description: With forearms on the wall, slide them up and finish by pushing the wall away to round the upper back slightly.
cues: Push through the forearms the whole way
Ribs stay down

exercises.name: Prone Y and T
exercises.description: Face down, lift the arms into a Y and then a T position with the thumbs up.
cues: Lift from the shoulder blade, not the hand
Bodyweight only at first

phases.name: Overhead Return
phases.goal: Restore pressing and overhead capacity with progressive load.
phases.advance_when: Overhead pressing is pain free and strength is close to symmetrical.

exercises.name: Incline Press
exercises.description: Press dumbbells from the shoulders on an incline bench, a friendlier angle than flat overhead.
cues: Shoulder blades set back and down
Stop short of a painful range

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Overhead Press
exercises.description: From a half-kneeling stance, press one dumbbell straight overhead.
cues: Squeeze the glute of the down leg
Do not let the ribs flare

exercises.name: Face Pull
exercises.description: Pull a band toward the face, finishing with the hands wide and the thumbs back.
cues: Elbows high
Pause one second at the finish

exercises.name: Overhead Carry
exercises.description: Hold a weight locked out overhead and walk with a tall posture.
cues: Elbow fully locked
Stop the set when the arm starts to drift forward

exercises.name: Push-Up Plus
exercises.description: At the top of a push-up, push the upper back toward the ceiling to spread the shoulder blades.
cues: The plus is a small, deliberate extra push
Start on an elevated surface if needed

ankle.name: Ankle
ankle.summary: Ankle rehab restores swelling control and motion, then rebuilds calf strength and balance, and finally retrains the hopping and cutting the ankle has to survive. Balance work is not optional: the reflexes that protect the ankle are what get lost after a sprain.
common_conditions: Chronic ankle instability and repeat rolling
precautions: Restoring dorsiflexion (knee travelling over the toes) is the single best predictor of a good outcome after a sprain.
Balance work should be done near a wall or counter you can grab.
With Achilles tendinopathy, favour slow, heavy heel raises and hold off on sudden jumping until the slow work is comfortable.
red_flags: Cannot bear weight for four steps right after the injury
Bony tenderness along the back edge of either ankle bone
A sudden pop at the back of the calf with a weak push-off, which can mean an Achilles rupture
Numbness or a cold, pale foot

phases.name: Protect and Move
phases.goal: Control swelling and restore ankle motion in all directions.
phases.advance_when: You can walk normally without a limp and swelling has largely settled.

exercises.name: Ankle Pump
exercises.description: Point and flex the foot through full range with the leg elevated.
cues: Elevate above heart height when you can
Rhythmic and continuous

exercises.name: Ankle Alphabet
exercises.description: Trace each letter of the alphabet in the air with the big toe.
cues: Move from the ankle, not the whole leg
Make the letters large

exercises.name: Isometric Eversion and Inversion
exercises.description: Press the outside, then inside, of the foot against a wall or your other foot without moving.
cues: Build the push over two seconds
No movement, just tension

exercises.name: Towel Calf Stretch
exercises.description: Seated with the leg straight, loop a towel around the ball of the foot and pull the toes toward you.
cues: Knee stays straight for the calf
Stretch, never sharp

exercises.name: Seated Heel Raise
exercises.description: Sitting with feet flat, lift the heels off the floor and lower slowly.
cues: Push through the big toe
Add a light weight on the knees when easy

phases.name: Strength and Balance
phases.goal: Rebuild calf and peroneal strength and restore single-leg balance.
phases.advance_when: You can hold single-leg balance 30 seconds with eyes closed and do 20 single-leg heel raises.

exercises.name: Band Eversion
exercises.description: With a band around the foot, turn the sole outward against resistance.
cues: Move only the foot, keep the knee still
Slow return every rep

exercises.name: Band Inversion
exercises.description: With the band anchored on the outside, turn the sole inward against resistance.
cues: Keep the leg fixed
Full controlled range

exercises.name: Knee-to-Wall Mobilization
exercises.description: With the toes a few inches from a wall, drive the knee forward over the toes keeping the heel down.
cues: Heel must stay flat
Track your distance from the wall week to week

exercises.name: Double to Single Leg Heel Raise
exercises.description: Rise onto the toes with both feet, then lower on the injured side alone.
cues: Full height at the top
Three seconds down

exercises.name: Single-Leg Balance
exercises.description: Stand on one leg with a soft knee, progressing from eyes open to eyes closed.
cues: Grip the floor with the toes
Stay near a counter

exercises.name: Heel and Toe Walks
exercises.description: Walk 20 metres on the heels, then 20 metres on the toes.
cues: Exaggerate the position
Stop if the shin cramps hard

phases.name: Power and Cutting
phases.goal: Restore elastic strength and the reactive control needed for sport.
phases.advance_when: Hopping and cutting are pain free and confident on both sides.

exercises.name: Slow Eccentric Single-Leg Heel Raise
exercises.description: Rise on one leg and lower over four seconds, ideally off the edge of a step.
cues: Four full seconds down
Add a backpack for load when easy

exercises.name: Star Excursion Reach
exercises.description: Balancing on one leg, reach the other foot as far as you can forward, diagonally back, and to the side.
cues: Reach light, do not transfer weight
Keep the standing heel down

exercises.name: Pogo Hop
exercises.description: Fast, small double-leg hops on the balls of the feet.
cues: Stiff ankles, quiet landings
Minimal ground contact time

exercises.name: Lateral Bound and Stick
exercises.description: Bound sideways onto one leg and hold the landing until completely still.
cues: Stick the landing for two seconds
Build distance gradually

exercises.name: Skipping Rope
exercises.description: Light continuous skipping to retrain rhythmic ankle stiffness.
cues: Land on the balls of the feet
Short bouts with full rest between

wrist.name: Wrist
wrist.summary: Wrist rehab starts with gentle motion and tendon gliding, builds grip and forearm strength in both directions, and ends with tolerating bodyweight through the hand. Most wrist and elbow tendon pain responds best to slow, heavy, controlled loading rather than rest alone.
common_conditions: Tennis elbow or golfer's elbow with wrist symptoms
Post-immobilization stiffness after a fracture, once cleared
Load-related pain from pressing, climbing, or keyboard work
precautions: Numbness or tingling in the thumb, index, and middle fingers suggests nerve involvement; back off aggressive stretching and get it assessed.
Build to weight-bearing on the hands gradually, starting with forearms or a fist before an open palm.
Train wrist flexors and extensors equally; grip work alone tends to make extensor pain worse.
red_flags: Pain in the hollow at the base of the thumb after a fall, which can mean a scaphoid fracture that is easy to miss
Visible deformity after a fall on an outstretched hand
Persistent numbness, night numbness, or thumb muscle wasting

phases.name: Settle and Mobilize
phases.goal: Restore comfortable motion in the wrist and fingers without provoking pain.
phases.advance_when: Full pain-free wrist bend and straighten, and everyday gripping is comfortable.

exercises.name: Tendon Glide
exercises.description: Move the fingers through straight, hook, fist, and tabletop positions in sequence.
cues: Pause briefly in each position
Smooth, no forcing

exercises.name: Wrist Flexion and Extension AROM
exercises.description: With the forearm supported on a table, move the hand up and down through comfortable range.
cues: Forearm stays down
Move only to the first resistance

exercises.name: Pronation and Supination
exercises.description: Elbow tucked at the side, turn the palm up and then down.
cues: Elbow stays glued to the ribs
Turn from the forearm, not the shoulder

exercises.name: Isometric Wrist Extension
exercises.description: Press the back of the hand up into the other hand without letting the wrist move.
cues: Build tension slowly
Aim for a mild, tolerable ache only

exercises.name: Median Nerve Glide
exercises.description: With the arm out to the side and palm up, gently extend the wrist and fingers, then release.
cues: This is a glide, never a hard stretch
Back off immediately if tingling increases

phases.name: Build Strength
phases.goal: Restore balanced forearm strength and grip endurance.
phases.advance_when: You can do light wrist curls in both directions for 15 reps without next-day soreness.

exercises.name: Wrist Extension Curl
exercises.description: Forearm resting on a table palm down, curl a light weight upward and lower slowly.
cues: Three seconds down every rep
Start with 1-2 pounds, it is enough

exercises.name: Wrist Flexion Curl
exercises.description: Forearm on a table palm up, curl the weight toward you and lower under control.
cues: Forearm stays down
Match the load you use for extension

exercises.name: Radial and Ulnar Deviation
exercises.description: With the thumb up, move the hand side to side against light resistance.
cues: Small range, this joint does not travel far
Keep the forearm still

exercises.name: Grip Squeeze
exercises.description: Squeeze a soft ball or grip trainer and hold.
cues: Full squeeze, full release
Stop if the outside of the elbow flares

exercises.name: Hammer Rotation
exercises.description: Hold a hammer or light dumbbell by the end and rotate the palm up and down against the weight.
cues: Choke up on the handle to make it easier
Control both directions

exercises.name: Finger Extension with Band
exercises.description: Place a rubber band around the fingertips and open the fingers against it.
cues: Spread all five digits
Slow close on the way back

phases.name: Load Bearing Return
phases.goal: Tolerate heavy grip and full bodyweight through the hand.
phases.advance_when: A full push-up on open palms and a 30 second hang are comfortable.

exercises.name: Heavy Slow Eccentric Wrist Extension
exercises.description: Lift the weight with both hands, then lower with the injured side alone over four seconds.
cues: The lowering is the whole exercise
Add load as long as it settles overnight

exercises.name: Quadruped Wrist Rock
exercises.description: On hands and knees, rock the body forward and back over the planted hands.
cues: Spread the fingers and press the knuckles down
Reduce the rock if the wrist pinches

exercises.name: Plank on Hands
exercises.description: Hold a high plank with straight arms, building the time you can tolerate.
cues: Push the floor away
Drop to forearms the moment the wrist complains

exercises.name: Farmer Carry
exercises.description: Walk carrying a heavy weight in each hand with a tall posture.
cues: Neutral wrist, do not let it bend back
Shoulders down

exercises.name: Dead Hang
exercises.description: Hang from a bar with a relaxed grip, building time gradually.
cues: Start with feet partly supported
Stop well before the grip fails
